export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b1-round2',
  description: 'B1 round two: apply the supervisor decisions (state-based outside detection, floor display rule, compare semantics, words), re-review with four lenses, verify findings, fix, re-check',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Fix2', detail: 'three fixers by ownership: store, site, docs' },
    { title: 'Review2', detail: 'store equality, browser, rules and clean-up audit, words' },
    { title: 'Verify2', detail: 'one skeptic per finding' },
    { title: 'Fix3', detail: 'fixers by ownership' },
    { title: 'Recheck2', detail: 'tests, builds, smoke, record' },
  ],
}

const WT = '/home/user/hail-b1/wt'
const BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-build-brief.md'
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b1/out2'
const CACHE = '/home/user/hail-b1/cache/mesh-backfill'
const PROTO_STORE = '/home/user/hail-b1/store/h1-mesh'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'
const OWNER = `The owner (Carson) wrote on 2026-10-18, verbatim: "Decisions that are mine. 1. Trailing 5 years to today. 2. A public lookup by typed address or clicked location. Each address in montana should have a dot to click on the map with a popup on each history of weather. 3. Pages only for now. 4. Make the weather updates consistent and recent as possible 5. Try to find and read hail units and codes then process it and make the user understand it easier. Where they can find the exact date that the hail happened at that location. 6. Don't include owners names. But I do want all addresses included and all types of weather at that address for the past 5 years in a popup after you click the house on the map. 7. Follow the laws"`

const DECISIONS = `SUPERVISOR DECISIONS FOR THIS ROUND (they override the brief where they differ; the brief at ${BRIEF} has them as items 10 to 16 under "Supervisor decisions for round 2", after items 1 to 9 of round 1):
10. One display rule: inches to two decimals, rounded down (floor), with the exact mm value: 513 tenths is "2.01 in (51.3 mm)", 185 is "0.72 in (18.5 mm)", 253 is "0.99 in (25.3 mm)", 190 is "0.74 in (19.0 mm)", 1015 is "3.99 in (101.5 mm)". No caps table: remove display_caps and display_hundredths; inches() returns the floored two-decimal string; map.js computes Math.floor(tenths * 100 / tenths_per_inch) / 100 and formats with two decimals. The words say "shown to the hundredth of an inch, rounded down, with the millimetre value exact". Update every example in docs, tests and the record (2.02 becomes 2.01; 0.73 becomes 0.72).
11. Outside-the-state is decided by the store. Shard format: {"f":"hail-cells-v1","r":..,"c":..,"d0":"2020-01-01","u":"tenths of a mm","state":[k,...],"cells":{"k":[[d,t],...]}} where state lists every in-tile key (0..99) of a Montana cell, sorted, and cells holds only keys with events. Every tile with at least one Montana cell gets a shard, even with no events. hail/index.json gets "tiles": ["r0790_c0199", ...] sorted; map.json["hail"] carries the same list under tiles (measure its bytes). Browser rule: tile name not in tiles means the outside words and no fetch; key not in the shard's state means the outside words; key in state with no entry in cells means the no-estimate words; otherwise the rows. The fixture follows the same format. tools/smoke_map.py checks Wyoming (43.5, -108.0), Idaho (44.6, -115.0) and Canada (49.5, -110.0): the outside words and zero shard requests; and an in-state cell with no events shows the no-estimate words after one fetch.
12. Compare gate and partial days: a re-derived day whose two-minute frames are incomplete is recorded in copy_check.partial as {"day": "2025-06-25", "frames": 717, "expected": 720} and still stored as the maximum of the frames that exist. compare passes when every non-re-derived overlapping day has 0 mismatches and every re-derived day equals the frame maximum the builder recorded; it prints the partial list. verify does not fail on partial days. copy_check keeps coverage, partial, frames, rederived, days_differed, days_checked, skipped.
13. The daily job installs like the site build: .github/workflows/hail-store.yml uses an unpinned pip line (pip install numpy pygrib requests); remove the version pins and the test that checks them.
14. Words. Day sentence: "A day runs from 12:00 UTC to 12:00 UTC the next day: 6 am to 6 am Mountain daylight time, 5 am to 5 am in winter (the SPC reporting day)." Cell sentence: "the largest hail over this cell, about 0.7 miles north to south and 0.5 miles east to west, during the day". Next-day sentence: "The newest day is added by a job that starts at 12:43 UTC and shows here on the next rebuild, usually within the hour." The contract row, DESIGN, About and D34 use the same sentences.
15. Gate texts in the record (research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b1-verification.json): B1-3: "the centre of the cell nearest Benchland that holds 513 tenths on SPC day 2025-06-15 (row 797, col 1986) shows 2.01 in (51.3 mm) on Jun 15, 2025; Benchland's own cell (792, 1998) shows 0.72 in (18.5 mm)". B1-5 per decision 12. B1-6: "the daily job is a full rebuild: a cold-cache and a warm-cache build give byte-identical shards, and the newest day re-decodes with 0 mismatches" (the append path is withdrawn). B1-1: the flag-off build may differ from the base build only in the shared static assets map.js and map.css and their ?v= hashes.
16. Test clean-up audit: every test under tests/ that calls rmtree, rm -rf, unlink or os.remove must act only on a path the test created (tempfile.mkdtemp or TemporaryDirectory inside the test).`

const COMMON = `You work in the git worktree ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b1; base commit 825d6c7; the B1 build and its first review round are in the working tree and in local WIP commits). Read ${BRIEF} in full first (the B1 interface spec, the round 1 and round 2 supervisor decisions). ${DECISIONS}
Repository rules that apply (AGENTS.md is in your context): Python first, evidence honesty, feed contracts, real-browser checks, no "best" claims, plain wording in sentence case, no em-dashes, no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names in repository files (branch names excepted), tests with every behaviour change, no new pip package for the site build (pyarrow only in compare, lazily). Edit only the files you own; other fixers are editing other files in the same worktree now, so never run git checkout, stash, reset, add, commit or push, never reformat a file you do not own, and never delete anything outside a folder you created under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ (a test's clean-up deleted the shared temporary directory's parent earlier today and wiped the session; do not repeat that). Return a plain report: what you changed, the commands you ran with results and measured numbers, and anything not done.`

const STORE_FIX = `${COMMON}

You are the store fixer. You own website/hail.py, tests/test_hail.py, .github/workflows/hail-store.yml and website/data/hail-fixture/. Apply decisions 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 to your files: (a) inches() floors to two decimals; remove display_caps and display_hundredths and every use; (b) the shard format gains "state" (sorted in-tile keys of Montana cells) and every tile with a Montana cell gets a shard even with no events; index.json gains "tiles"; map_data() passes tiles through (and keep tenths_per_inch 254); describe() and cell_events() distinguish outside (key not in state), no events and rows; (c) compare: pass when non-re-derived days have 0 mismatches and re-derived days equal the recorded frame maximum; print partial days; verify does not fail on partial; copy_check keeps coverage, partial, frames, rederived, days_differed, days_checked, skipped; (d) hail-store.yml: unpinned pip line, drop the pin test; (e) WORDS: the three sentences of decision 14 and the display sentence of decision 10 in what_this_is and source. Regenerate the fixture FIRST (within your first steps, so the site fixer can use it): website/data/hail-fixture/ in the new format with the real decoded values for its tiles (the Benchland tile r0079_c0199 and the 513 cell's tile (row 797, col 1986) if different, plus the Billings tile), labelled sample; keep it under 50 KB. Then update tests (floor rule examples: 513 to "2.01", 185 to "0.72", 253 to "0.99", 190 to "0.74", 1015 to "3.99", 254 to "1.00", 64 to "0.25"; state keys; zero-event shards; tiles; compare semantics; partial handling; no pins) and make python -m unittest tests.test_hail pass under the system python and under ${VENV}. Then rebuild the real store: python -m website.hail build --out ${OUT}/store/store --cache ${CACHE} --procs 6 (network for the newest stamps and the copy-rule HEADs), verify, compare --prototype ${PROTO_STORE} (pyarrow under ${VENV}), tar czf ${OUT}/store/hail-store.tar.gz -C ${OUT}/store/store hail. Measure and report: shards (expect about 4,597 now), events, bytes of hail/, the largest shard, the bytes of the tiles list, wall time, copy_check contents, compare output, partial days.`

const SITE_FIX = `${COMMON}

You are the site fixer. You own website/build.py, website/sources.py, website/templates/ (map.html, town.html, about.html), website/static/map/map.js, website/static/map/map.css, tools/smoke_map.py, tests/test_site.py and .github/workflows/website.yml. The store fixer is changing website/hail.py at the same time (read it, import it, never edit it); it regenerates website/data/hail-fixture/ in the new format early: poll for the "tiles" key in website/data/hail-fixture/hail/index.json every 2 minutes for up to 30 minutes while you work on the browser code. Apply: (a) decision 10 in map.js: Math.floor(tenths * 100 / tenths_per_inch) / 100 formatted to two decimals; remove the caps logic; (b) decision 11 in map.js: the tiles list from map.json.hail.tiles (a Set), the shard's state list, the three outcomes (outside without fetch, outside after fetch when the key is not in state, no-estimate when in state without events, rows otherwise), no polygon in the browser; build.py passes tiles from the index into map.json["hail"]; (c) decision 14 and the display sentence in website/sources.py CONTRACTS["hail_history"] and about.html (the words in hail.py WORDS are the store fixer's; the templates and the contract are yours; use the same sentences); (d) tools/smoke_map.py: the outside checks of decision 11 (Wyoming 43.5,-108.0; Idaho 44.6,-115.0; Canada 49.5,-110.0: outside words, zero shard requests; an in-state no-events cell shows the no-estimate words after one fetch; the Benchland gate per decision 15 at the centre of row 797, col 1986: "2.01 in (51.3 mm)" and "Jun 15, 2025"; Benchland's own cell 792,1998: "0.72 in (18.5 mm)"); (e) tests/test_site.py updated for the new format, the floor rule, the tiles key, the forbidden map.js strings; (f) nothing else changes in website.yml unless the flag line needs it. Run python -m unittest tests.test_site (and the full suite at the end), build --sample (flag off), --hail-history --sample, and when ${OUT}/store/hail-store.tar.gz exists (poll every 2 minutes up to 40 minutes), --hail-history --sample --hail-store that tar, into ${OUT}/site/{off,sample,real}; run PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium python tools/smoke_map.py on each (--shots on the real one) and quote the results. Report what you changed and measured.`

const DOCS_FIX = `${COMMON}

You are the docs fixer. You own docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, README.md, AGENTS.md and research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b1-verification.json. Apply decisions 10, 11, 12, 14 and 15 to the docs: the display rule and its examples (2.01, 0.72, 0.99), the state-based outside rule and the shard and index formats (DESIGN data contract), the compare and partial-day semantics (D34 and the record), the three sentences of decision 14 (D34, DESIGN), the record's gate texts (decision 15: B1-1, B1-3, B1-5, B1-6) with status "pending" until the re-check fills them, and keep D34's verbatim quotation of the owner's seven sentences unchanged (${OWNER}). Check README.md and AGENTS.md lines for the B1 flag and the daily job still match. Em-dashes 0 in your lines; no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names; no invented measurements (write "measured in the re-check" where a number is pending). Report the diff stat of your files.`

const FINDINGS = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, file: { type: 'string' }, line: { type: 'integer' }, claim: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, fix: { type: 'string' },
      severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocking', 'should', 'minor'] }, confidence: { type: 'number' } },
      required: ['id', 'file', 'line', 'claim', 'evidence', 'fix', 'severity', 'confidence'] } },
    measurements: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true },
    gates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { gate: { type: 'string' }, status: { type: 'string', enum: ['pass', 'fail', 'not_checked'] }, evidence: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['gate', 'status', 'evidence'] } },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['findings', 'measurements', 'gates', 'summary'],
}
const VERDICT = { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, refuted: { type: 'boolean' }, reason: { type: 'string' }, fix_ok: { type: 'boolean' }, adjusted_fix: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'refuted', 'reason', 'fix_ok', 'adjusted_fix'] }

const REVIEW_COMMON = `Read-only reviewer in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b1; base 825d6c7). Read ${BRIEF} first (spec, round 1 and round 2 decisions). ${DECISIONS} Never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ which you create; never delete anything outside it. Report concrete defects only, each with file, line, evidence (command output or quoted text) and an exact minimal fix; rank blocking first; fill the gates you checked; put every measured number in measurements.`

const REVIEWERS = [
  { key: 'store', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the store after round 2. Read website/hail.py and tests/test_hail.py in full against the spec and decisions 10 to 13. Check the shard format (state keys, zero-event shards for every Montana tile: count tiles with Montana cells from the mask and compare with the shard count and the tiles list), the index (tiles, copy_check keys incl. coverage and partial), inches() floor examples (513 "2.01", 185 "0.72", 253 "0.99", 190 "0.74", 1015 "3.99", 254 "1.00", 64 "0.25"), class edges vs display (no displayed value crosses its class edge over 64..10000 tenths; write and run the script), describe() outcomes (outside, no events, rows, stale, sample), fetch_store and load_store safety (bad hash, non-tar, traversal, unlisted files), compare semantics (run it on ${OUT}/store/store against ${PROTO_STORE} with ${VENV} and quote the output), verify, the workflow YAML (parse; unpinned pip line; cron; permissions; concurrency; release commands), and an independent re-decode of three stamps from ${CACHE} compared with the shards (0 mismatches). Gates: store equals the prototype on every non-re-derived overlapping day and equals the frame maximum on re-derived days; hail/ at most 60 MB; verify ok; the 513 cell (797,1986) and Benchland's cell (792,1998) hold 513 and 185 on 2025-06-15.` },
  { key: 'browser', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the site in Chromium (rule 8). Build from a copy, never from the worktree in place: cp -r ${WT} ${OUT}/browser/src (exclude .git) and build there: --sample --now 2026-10-18T12:00:00Z (flag off) into ${OUT}/browser/off, --hail-history --sample into ${OUT}/browser/sample, --hail-history --sample --hail-store ${OUT}/store/hail-store.tar.gz into ${OUT}/browser/real; and the BASE build from git -C ${WT} archive 825d6c7 | tar -x -C ${OUT}/browser/base-src into ${OUT}/browser/base-off; diff -rq base-off vs off: only static/map/map.js, static/map/map.css and the ?v= lines in pages may differ (decision 5); anything else is blocking. Serve the real build with python -m http.server and with Playwright (PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium; read tools/smoke_map.py for the harness): run tools/smoke_map.py and quote the result; then your own probes: the centre of cell row 797 col 1986 shows "2.01 in (51.3 mm)" and "Jun 15, 2025"; the centre of cell 792,1998 shows "0.72 in (18.5 mm)"; Wyoming (43.5,-108.0), Idaho (44.6,-115.0), Canada (49.5,-110.0) and the Pacific (40,-130) show the outside words with zero shard requests (log every request host and path); an in-state cell with no events shows the no-estimate words after one fetch; ?at= opens on arrival and is dropped on Escape and on Close (reload does not reopen); every request goes to the local server only; screenshots at 390x844 and 1280x800, light and dark, into ${OUT}/browser/shots, open them and describe; town pages: Billings' table rows match an independent read of the store (two decimals, floored); the flag-off build has no sheet markup, no hail key, no hail/ folder and a click does nothing; tools/smoke_pages.py on the real build. Read map.js's hail section: list any literal that is a threshold, unit, class word or sentence (none expected; the 100 and the 2 of the formatting are allowed) and check the header documents the duty.` },
  { key: 'rules', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: repository rules over the whole diff (git -C ${WT} diff 825d6c7 --stat, the full diff, untracked files). Check: Python first; evidence honesty (no damage, "no hail" as fact outside the negation sentences, all-clear, insurance, eligibility; missing said as missing; the kind named; SAMPLE labels); the contract row's units, timing, cadence, missing rules, copy rule, units table match the code and decision 14; tests exist for every behaviour change; python -m unittest discover -s tests passes (run it, quote the tail) and python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload passes; website.yml passes the flag only on branch previews and runs tests.test_hail; the daily workflow is sound and unpinned; docs match what was built (D34 quotes the owner's seven sentences verbatim: compare character by character with ${OWNER}; DESIGN, ROADMAP, README, AGENTS make no unmeasured claim); the display rule examples in docs are floored (2.01, 0.72, 0.99); em-dashes in added lines 0; the words Claude, Anthropic, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI, Copilot, Gemini, Haiku, Opus, Sonnet in added lines only inside branch names; plain wording and sentence case; no new pip package; no hex colours; fixture under 50 KB and labelled sample. DECISION 16 AUDIT: grep every file under tests/ for rmtree, "rm -rf", unlink, os.remove, shutil.rmtree and TemporaryDirectory/mkdtemp; for each deletion, show the path expression and prove it is a directory the test created; any deletion of a parent, a shared temp root or a path derived from an output's parent is a blocking finding.` },
  { key: 'words', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: words and sizes after round 2. (1) NWS chart: the live NWS spotter chart (weather.gov/fsd/spotter or another NWS office's hail size table) vs CLASSES words and inch values; "mothball" is not on the NWS copies read in round 1, so check whether the class word for 0.25 to 0.74 in should read "pea to marble" or similar per the chart you can read; cite the page. (2) The floor rule: run inches() over 64..10200 tenths and check no displayed value crosses its class edge, and the examples. (3) Read every WORDS value, the templates, the About paragraph, DESIGN's words and the contract row for forbidden terms (damage, damaged, dry, clear, insurance, eligible, confirmed; "no hail" only inside the negation sentences), plain words, sentence case, the three sentences of decision 14 used verbatim everywhere, the display sentence of decision 10, "estimate is not an inspection", the stale and unavailable lines (the unavailable line must say "This is not the same as no hail."), SAMPLE labels; the store-error texts a visitor can see hold no forbidden term. (4) describe() on the fixture's 513 cell, on an outside key, on an in-state empty cell, on a stale index: quote the output; placeholders in WORDS match the keys map.js fills; no unfilled brace in the rendered sample build's hail sections.` },
]

const OWNERSHIP = {
  store: ['website/hail.py', 'tests/test_hail.py', '.github/workflows/hail-store.yml', 'website/data/hail-fixture/'],
  site: ['website/build.py', 'website/sources.py', 'website/templates/', 'website/static/map/map.js', 'website/static/map/map.css', 'tools/smoke_map.py', 'tests/test_site.py', '.github/workflows/website.yml'],
  docs: ['docs/', 'README.md', 'AGENTS.md', 'research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b1-verification.json'],
}
function ownerOf(file) {
  for (const [k, prefixes] of Object.entries(OWNERSHIP)) if (prefixes.some((p) => file.startsWith(p) || file.includes(p))) return k
  return 'site'
}

phase('Fix2')
const fixes2 = await parallel([
  () => agent(STORE_FIX, { label: 'fix2:store', phase: 'Fix2', model: 'haiku' }),
  () => agent(SITE_FIX, { label: 'fix2:site', phase: 'Fix2', model: 'haiku' }),
  () => agent(DOCS_FIX, { label: 'fix2:docs', phase: 'Fix2', model: 'haiku' }),
])
const [storeR, siteR, docsR] = fixes2
log(`fix2 done: store ${storeR ? 'ok' : 'null'}, site ${siteR ? 'ok' : 'null'}, docs ${docsR ? 'ok' : 'null'}`)

phase('Review2')
const reviews = await pipeline(
  REVIEWERS,
  (r) => agent(`${r.prompt}\n\nFixer reports for context (claims to check, not facts):\nSTORE: ${(storeR || 'none').slice(0, 6000)}\nSITE: ${(siteR || 'none').slice(0, 6000)}\nDOCS: ${(docsR || 'none').slice(0, 3000)}`, { label: `review2:${r.key}`, phase: 'Review2', schema: FINDINGS, model: 'haiku' }),
  async (result, r) => {
    if (!result) return { key: r.key, findings: [], measurements: {}, gates: [], summary: 'reviewer returned nothing' }
    const fs = result.findings.map((f, i) => ({ ...f, id: `${r.key}-${i + 1}` }))
    log(`${r.key}: ${fs.length} findings`)
    const verdicts = await parallel(fs.map((f) => () =>
      agent(`You are a skeptic checking one review finding in ${WT} (read-only; never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/skeptic-${f.id}/ which you create). The finding:\n${JSON.stringify(f, null, 1)}\n\nOpen the file at the line, reproduce the observation yourself, and read ${BRIEF} (spec and the round 1 and round 2 decisions). ${DECISIONS}\nThe finding stands only if the defect is real, matters to the gates, the decisions or the repository rules (AGENTS.md), and the proposed fix is correct and minimal and introduces nothing unsupported (no new number, no em-dash, no model or AI-product name, no new pip package, no scope widening, no contradiction of a supervisor decision). If the defect is real but the fix is wrong or too broad, set fix_ok false and give an adjusted_fix. Default to refuted=true when uncertain.`,
        { label: `verify2:${f.id}`, phase: 'Verify2', schema: VERDICT, model: 'haiku' })
        .then((v) => (v ? { ...f, verdict: v } : null))))
    return { key: r.key, findings: verdicts.filter(Boolean), measurements: result.measurements, gates: result.gates, summary: result.summary }
  },
)

const all = reviews.flatMap((r) => r.findings)
const confirmed = all.filter((f) => !f.verdict.refuted).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, file: f.file, line: f.line, claim: f.claim, evidence: f.evidence, severity: f.severity, fix: f.verdict.fix_ok ? f.fix : f.verdict.adjusted_fix, owner: ownerOf(f.file) })).filter((f) => f.fix && f.fix.length > 0)
const refuted = all.filter((f) => f.verdict.refuted).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, file: f.file, claim: f.claim, reason: f.verdict.reason }))
log(`confirmed ${confirmed.length} (blocking ${confirmed.filter((f) => f.severity === 'blocking').length}), refuted ${refuted.length}`)

phase('Fix3')
const groups = ['store', 'site', 'docs'].map((k) => ({ k, items: confirmed.filter((f) => f.owner === k) })).filter((g) => g.items.length)
const fix3 = await parallel(groups.map((g) => () =>
  agent(`${COMMON}\n\nYou are the round-3 fixer for the ${g.k} files; you own exactly: ${OWNERSHIP[g.k].join(', ')}. Apply these confirmed findings with exact, minimal edits that keep every public name and the supervisor decisions. Skip and report any finding naming a file you do not own. After editing run python -m unittest tests.test_hail tests.test_site (and the full suite if you changed hail.py or build.py); if a fix changes the store format, rebuild ${OUT}/store/store and the tar with the store fixer's commands and say so. Report applied ids, skipped ids with reasons, and the test tail.\n\nFINDINGS:\n${JSON.stringify(g.items, null, 1)}`,
    { label: `fix3:${g.k}`, phase: 'Fix3', model: 'haiku' })))

phase('Recheck2')
const recheck = await agent(`${REVIEW_COMMON} You are the final checker. Run and quote: python -m unittest discover -s tests (tail); python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload; builds from a copy of the worktree (cp -r ${WT} ${OUT}/recheck/src without .git): --sample --now 2026-10-18T12:00:00Z into ${OUT}/recheck/off, --hail-history --sample into ${OUT}/recheck/sample, --hail-history --sample --hail-store ${OUT}/store/hail-store.tar.gz into ${OUT}/recheck/real; PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium python tools/smoke_map.py on each (--shots on the real one) and tools/smoke_pages.py on the real one; du -sb hail/ in the real build and each _site; the largest shard; the bytes of map.json and of its tiles list; python -m website.hail verify ${OUT}/store/store and compare against ${PROTO_STORE} with ${VENV}; git -C ${WT} status --short and diff --stat 825d6c7; em-dash and banned-name counts over added lines; a grep of the built real pages for an unfilled brace inside hail sections; the decision 16 audit result. Then update research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b1-verification.json in ${WT} (the one file you may edit): each gate's status and evidence from what you measured (gate texts per decision 15), measurements, and the confirmed findings applied and refuted ones (ids, one line each) under notes. Return the gate table and measurements as JSON text.`,
  { label: 'recheck2', phase: 'Recheck2', model: 'haiku' })

return { storeR: (storeR || '').slice(0, 6000), siteR: (siteR || '').slice(0, 6000), docsR: (docsR || '').slice(0, 3000), reviews: reviews.map((r) => ({ key: r.key, summary: r.summary, gates: r.gates, measurements: r.measurements })), confirmed, refuted, fix3, recheck }

result.storeR:
The store fixer's work is finished, and the code, tests, fixture and build outputs are in place. Nothing was committed or pushed. The main open issue is that in a `--sample` build, 13 of the 14 towns would read "Outside Montana", which needs a decision from you.

**Files changed (worktree /home/user/hail-b1/wt)**
